newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Brent to consolidate before further gain.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Brent to consolidate before further gain.

text.p: ----------------- VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - May 19 -------------- * Analysts are looking for Brent to "build volume" around these new higher levels to confirm the fresh gains. * Prices to stage a pullback to under Friday's close in early trade with strong support in play at 20.04.

IPE Brent crude oil futures are expected to consolidate around $20 with the market initially settling back after soaring to two-month highs as institutional funds bought up WTI futures in the United States and on technical factors, analysts said.
The front month July Brent contract last traded at $20.35 a barrel, up 86 cents on Friday, while in New York July paper last traded at $22.10, up a hefty 80 cents on the day.
Both contracts broke through stubborn resistance levels while Brent hit levels not seen since March 19, when it briefly traded at $20.84.

Analysts are looking for Brent to "build volume" around these new higher levels to confirm the fresh gains although some were more sceptical that funds buying on Friday were the main force driving the gains.
"33,000 is relatively low volume. I would have expected fund-related buying to have push the volume up a lot higher than that," Fenella Graham at Mees Pierson in London said.
The rise continues a remarkable bull run begun two weeks ago, which saw crude break out of the $17.50-$18.50 range it was stuck in after falling sharply from early year highs of $25.
Friday's close was just above last year's average price of $20.32, a level many analysts had regarded as was unreachable in current conditions of plentiful supply and poor demand.

"We have a technical breakout. It could be an ascending triangle or a pennant. Call it what you will. It adds up to the same thing," said energy analyst Thomas Blakeslee at Cargill Investor services in New York.
"Last time we were in this territory we moved quite fast. I won't be able to tell where the top is until at least an hour after opening on Monday morning," said one broker.
Al Graham at Elliott Wave International said he looked for prices stage a pullback to under Friday's close in early trade with strong support in play at $20.04.
